title: One Open Insurance Claim Repairs Repair Order per Claim and Vehicle
content:
## Clause

One insurer claim number may have at most the class's limit of open Insurance Claim Repairs repair orders on one vehicle — one in every class. A repair order is **open** in any status other than closed, cancelled or total loss.

A repair order is opened only when no open repair order exists for the same vehicle and insurer claim number. This is read from the system's repair order records before the repair order is opened, matching on the vehicle together with the insurer claim number.

Further damage found on the same claim is handled as a supplement on the open repair order, never as a second repair order. A Customer-Pay Repairs repair is never opened for a vehicle with an open claim repair order; customer-pay work on that vehicle is added to the claim repair order as a customer-pay addition.

## Status table

| Status of an existing repair order for the same vehicle and claim number | Counts as open |
|---|---|
| assigned | Yes |
| authorized | Yes |
| in repair | Yes |
| on hold | Yes |
| repair complete | Yes |
| delivered | Yes |
| closed | No |
| cancelled | No |
| total loss | No |

## Applying the clause (hypothetical records)

- The same vehicle has a delivered repair order under the same claim number: that repair order is open, so no new repair order opens for that vehicle and claim number.
- The same vehicle has a cancelled repair order under the same claim number, and nothing else: no open repair order exists for the pair, so the condition is met.
- The same vehicle has an in-repair order under a **different** claim number: the match requires both the vehicle and the claim number, so that repair order does not count against this claim number.
- Hidden damage is found on a vehicle whose repair order under the claim is on hold: it is written as a supplement on that repair order.
